title: Open for the season (the signboard)
caption:
Every Indian town has a matching centre. This season, Naira is one.

Twelve posts, twelve shades, Karwa Chauth to the first muhurat. Shade N° 01 is the red: the Baguette Tennis Bracelet in ruby-red cubic zirconia, ₹1,599.

Send a photo of what you’re wearing on WhatsApp, +91 95615 57935, and we’ll send back three matches with photographs.

[ baguette tennis bracelet · 18k gold tone plated · matched to the red ]
first_comment:
Five of the swatches on slide 2 are Naira Flore couture, made to measure in Nashik. Free insured shipping. COD available. Every piece arrives in the Naira gift box.
#NairaFlore #NairaPetite #MatchingCentre #EditionTwo #DemiFineJewellery
alt_text: A blush pink tile. A painted sage-green shop signboard, with a screw in each corner, reads NAIRA, Matching Centre, and the same words in Marathi. Under it, in italics: every piece, matched to an outfit, an evening or a person. Below, a fan of five fabric swatches with zigzag pinked edges in purple with a woven border, green, turmeric yellow, ivory and ruby red. A gold-tone tennis bracelet of ruby-red baguette stones lies on the red swatch, knotted at its clasp to a fine thread that runs to an ivory hang-tag with a ruby top reading Shade N° 01, matched to the red, ruby-red cubic zirconia.

An ivory tile. A small heading reads Matching Centre, with the same words in Marathi. Large capitals: Every town has one. In italics below: the shop where a saree goes in, and comes out with its blouse piece, its fall and its petticoat. A row of seven pinned fabric swatches with pinked edges: plain ruby red; marigold georgette with an embroidered sprig; pale pink with chevrons; navy with pale embroidered florals; a tree print with sequinned blossoms; a printed lehenga panel showing an elephant under a flowering arch; and plain Paithani purple with a woven border. Under them, in italics: five of these swatches are our own couture. Then: Naira began as a couture house in Nashik. This season, its jewellery counter does the matching.

A blush tile. Small type at the top reads Matching Centre, how it works. Headed How it works, with three numbered rows. 01, beside a pinned ruby-red swatch: Show us the outfit, or a photo of it, on WhatsApp. 02, beside a small paper shade card of six chips in ruby, green, ivory, purple, gold tone and silver tone: We match the shade, four stone shades, two metal tones, wherever the piece comes in them. 03, beside the closed blush Naira gift box: It leaves in the box, every piece arrives in our gift box. At the foot, on two lines: WhatsApp +91 95615 57935; Monday to Saturday, 10 am to 7 pm.

A deep sage-green tile headed One sign, five languages. Five cream shop boards, each with a fine gold-coloured rule and four small screw heads, read Matching Centre in Marathi, Hindi, Kannada, Tamil and Telugu. Under each board, its language and the cities it stands for: Marathi, Nashik, Mumbai, Pune; Hindi, Delhi NCR; Kannada, Bengaluru; Tamil, Chennai; Telugu, Hyderabad. At the foot, in blush italics: one sign, in the languages of the homes our parcels went to.

A blush tile. Small type at the top reads Matching Centre, the series. Headed On the counter this season. Four rows divided by fine gold-coloured rules, each beside a small hang-tag with a window of the series colour and a faint blush flower. The Match: one piece, matched to one evening, posts N° 02, 04, 06, 10 and 11. Shade Card: every colour a piece comes in, N° 07 and 08. Maap, written in Marathi, The Measurements: what it is, exactly, in millimetres, N° 05 and 09. The Sample Blouse: matching for someone who won’t say, N° 03. At the foot: which evening are you dressing for first? Tell us in the comments.
